newsitem.title: USA: IBM to sell high-speed networking chips.
newsitem.headline: IBM to sell high-speed networking chips.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp said that it plans to sell on the open market for the first time several high-performance networking chips, chips that IBM previously used for internal consumption.

IBM said it will market its ATM (asynchronous transfer mode), Ethernet and Token Ring chips, and associated application specific integrated circuit functions, to networking hardware equipment manufacturers.
IBM also said it will sell an innovative ATM switching technology that enables smooth transmission of data, voice and video at speeds of up to 155 megabits per second.

IBM said that Dataquest Inc, a San Jose, Calif.-based market research firm, is forecasting the current communications market opportunity at $30 billion and that the market will double in the next four years.
IBM is pursuing the networking, or wired communications segment, which is the largest portion of that market.
The networking chips are being sold through IBM's Microelectronics division's direct sales force and through a worldwide network of IBM distributors. The chips are available immediately.
